chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
One who cheats a Muslim, causes him harm, or plots against him is not from among us.

key_terms.ضَرَّهُ: To cause him harm or injury
key_terms.ماكَرَهُ: To plot against him or act with cunning

ai.seo_question: What are the three actions that disqualify a person from being considered part of the Prophet's community according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith establishes a triad of social vices—deception (*ghash*), harm (*darr*), and scheming (*makar*)—as disqualifiers from the Prophet’s community. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (character) as a definitive marker of *usul al-din*, linking personal integrity directly to communal identity and spiritual belonging.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-26 According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said, “
One who cheats a Muslim, causes him any losses, or plots against him is not from among my nation.”
